verdicts.evidence: HEADER-CAVEAT FAMILY (this mutant and the two below it). The pack's header blockquote is where the document states what it is and what the regime is; emptying one of its lines deletes a claim a reader acts on and nothing notices. RECIPE: any mission — `runward init`, then `runward compliance nist-ai-rmf`. Before, line 4 of runward/compliance/nist-ai-rmf-readiness.md reads `> deterministically from ratified engineering artifacts (no model call). The AI RMF is **voluntary guidance**`. After, that line is empty. Two claims go with it. (1) The provenance claim: the document no longer says the pack was assembled deterministically from artifacts at rest with no model call — the one statement telling a regulated buyer this is not model output, in a framework whose whole pitch is that nothing here was generated. (2) The regime's legal character: the AI RMF is voluntary guidance, and with the qualifier gone the document reads as an assessment against a binding standard. The blank also terminates the blockquote, so the surviving opening sentence ('… Assembled by `runward compliance nist-ai-rmf` on <date>,') is left with no predicate and the next line resumes as a separate quote beginning 'with no pass/fail and no certification;', now attached to nothing. All twelve assertions still pass on the mutant output — /Draft/ and 'not a compliance claim' are on line 3, which this mutant does not touch.

verdicts.evidence: EQUIVALENT, with the control. Measured: byte-identical output on all three fixtures — the diff is empty, not merely 'looks the same'. Reachability: renderNistAiRmf has exactly one caller, REGIMES['nist-ai-rmf'] in src/commands/compliance.ts, which passes lens = loadRegime('nist-ai-rmf', opts.regimeVersion). loadRegime resolves the requested version against the shipped catalogue and throws — mapped to exit 2 by the command — for anything not in it (`versions.includes(pick)`), and the catalogue for this regime is exactly one file, regimes/nist-ai-rmf@1.0.json, which defines crosswalk.primary. So on every input runward can be given, lens.crosswalk is an object and the `?.` never short-circuits. SENSITIVITY CONTROL — the nearby input on which the two WOULD differ: a second shipped mapping, regimes/nist-ai-rmf@2.0.json (ADR-0022: an AI RMF update is a new file, never an edit of a shipped one), written without a `crosswalk` key. The shipped code then emits the literal word 'undefined' into a pack a regulated buyer reads; the mutant throws TypeError and the command dies. Why it cannot occur: the catalogue is packaged data resolved from PKG_ROOT (package.json ships `regimes/`), never from the mission, so no operator input reaches it — adding a file means editing the installed package — and test/unit/compliance.test.js:225 ('no lens field may render as undefined') is the assertion that keeps the shipped set complete. Worth recording rather than hiding: the `?.` is not redundant defence, it is what would turn a future incomplete lens into a silent 'undefined' in a compliance document instead of a crash, and of those two the crash is the better failure.
